_note: Facts the Skeptic may cite. Each rule links to Microsoft Learn. Drafted with AI help at build time; set verified=true after a human checks the linked page.

rules.fact: Function executions time out after 5 minutes by default and at most 10 minutes; HTTP-triggered functions must respond within 230 seconds.
Apps scale to zero when idle, so the first request after idle has a cold start delay.
The Consumption plan does not support virtual network integration; Flex Consumption, Premium and Dedicated plans do.

Container Apps can scale to zero replicas; the first request after scale-in waits for a replica to start (cold start). Set minimum replicas >= 1 to avoid it (idle replicas are billed at the lower idle rate).
A replica on the Consumption profile can use at most 4 vCPU and 8 GiB memory; larger needs a Dedicated workload profile.
Requests that take longer than 230 seconds are cut off by the App Service front end; long work must run in the background.
Free and Shared tiers run on shared VMs with CPU quotas, have no SLA and are meant for development and testing, not production.
Basic plans support manual scale-out only (no autoscale) and no deployment slots; autoscale and slots start at Standard.

rules.applies_to: Spot VMs and Spot node pools
rules.fact: Spot VMs can be evicted at any time when Azure needs the capacity or the price exceeds your max, and have no SLA. Only for interruptible work.
B-series VMs earn CPU credits below a baseline and spend them to burst; sustained high CPU drops to the baseline once credits run out. Not for steady high-CPU loads.
The AKS Free tier has no financially backed uptime SLA for the API server; the Standard tier adds the Uptime SLA and is recommended for production.

rules.applies_to: General Purpose serverless with auto-pause enabled
rules.fact: Serverless databases can auto-pause after an idle delay; the first connection after a pause waits while the database resumes, which can take up to about a minute.
The Basic DTU tier allows a maximum database size of 2 GB and 5 DTUs; only for very small, light databases.
High availability (zone-redundant or same-zone standby) is not supported on the Burstable tier; use General Purpose or Memory Optimized when HA is required.
High availability is not supported on the Burstable tier; use General Purpose or Business Critical when HA is required.
The Basic tier is a single node with no replication and no SLA; it is for development and testing. Standard adds a replica and an SLA.
Data persistence, clustering and virtual network injection need the Premium tier (or higher); Basic and Standard lack them.
Event Hubs Basic allows one consumer group, one day of event retention, and no Capture. Capture (writing events straight to storage) needs Standard or higher.
Data residency: resources must run in one of the run's allowed regions. Moving to a region outside the allowed list breaks the requirement.
